Iran International live, 26 Nov

Israel’s military is ready to strike Iran on its own, military spokesman Effie Defrin told Israeli public broadcaster Kan on Thursday.

The head of Iran’s Basij paramilitary force called for spreading its ideology and its vision of “resistance” worldwide, describing that as the next step after the domestic goal of making “every Iranian a Basij member.”

Belgian Defense Minister Theo Francken on Thursday condemned Iran’s use of flogging and executions against women and protesters, criticizing Western media for their coverage of the Islamic Republic’s human rights abuses.

Iranian truck drivers entered a fifth day of strikes on Thursday, with their union saying drivers in 18 cities were refusing to haul freight at rates that have stayed flat as the cost of keeping a truck on the road has climbed.

Iran is rapidly constructing a fortified underground complex between two of its main nuclear sites that could house weapons systems or infrastructure linked to its nuclear program, a Washington-based research institute said on Wednesday.

Iran’s military on Thursday denied attacking a facility in Kuwait, and its embassy in Rome warned of “false flag” operations after two Italian nationals were killed in a reported drone strike there.

Brigadier General Abolfazl Shekarchi, spokesman for Iran’s armed forces, rejected the Kuwaiti military’s allegation that Iranian forces had attacked one of the country’s vital facilities. He said Iranian forces had carried out no military operation in the area.

In a separate statement, the embassy denied Iranian responsibility for the strike and said “false flag” operations were aimed at widening the conflict in the Persian Gulf and drawing Europe into it.

100%Iran's military spokesman Abolfazl ShekarchiNov 26, 2026, 15:52 GMT+0Von der Leyen urges more pressure on Iran after drone strike kills two ItaliansEuropean Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called on Thursday for greater pressure on Iran to end its attacks on its Persian Gulf neighbors after an Iranian drone strike killed two Italian nationals in Kuwait.

“We must step up pressure on Iran to put an end to these unacceptable attacks against its neighbors and our partners in the [Persian] Gulf,” von der Leyen said. She added that security in the Persian Gulf “is a matter of security for us all.”

Writing in Italian, von der Leyen said her thoughts were with the victims’ loved ones and the Italian people.

Kuwait on Thursday condemned an Iranian drone attack on its “vital sites” and said it reserved the right to take all necessary measures to defend its territory and protect key facilities.

The attack killed two Italian nationals, wounded a Kuwaiti citizen and a Pakistani national, and caused property damage, Kuwait’s foreign ministry said.

The ministry accused Iran of violating Kuwait’s sovereignty, the UN Charter and UN Security Council Resolution 2817. It warned that continued Iranian attacks threatened regional stability and undermined diplomatic efforts to ease tensions.

Kuwait cited its right to self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. It also offered condolences to Italy’s government and people.

Iran’s army has developed new defense equipment since the recent war, with its deployment inflicting significant damage on the “enemy,” army chief of staff and coordinating deputy Habibollah Sayyari said on Thursday.

The army continues to design and produce new air defense systems, and adversaries would face its enhanced defensive capabilities in the event of another attack, Sayyari added.

Two Italian employees of German defense company Rheinmetall have died from injuries sustained in an Iranian attack on Kuwait, Italian news agency ANSA reported on Thursday.

Four people were injured in a drone attack on what Kuwait’s Defense Ministry described as a vital site on Thursday.

The ministry blamed Iran and said Kuwaiti forces detected several drones in the country’s airspace and responded.

German federal police arrested two Iraqi nationals on Thursday on suspicion of belonging to a pro-Iranian terrorist group that prosecutors say plotted attacks on synagogues in Cologne and another European city.

Unidentified people acting on the group’s behalf went to the synagogues on two consecutive nights in late March, “presumably carrying explosive devices,” federal prosecutors said.

Neither attack took place, and investigators said they still did not know why.

Police arrested the two men, identified as Mostafa Al-R. and Ameer J., in Heidelberg and Cologne.

Prosecutors said both were “strongly suspected of membership in a domestic terrorist organization.”

According to the arrest warrants, Mostafa Al-R. and Mohammad al-Saadi, who faces charges in the United States, founded the group with others in late 2025 to prepare and carry out attacks in Germany and elsewhere in Europe.

South Korea will stay out of the US-Iran war, Foreign Minister Cho Hyun told his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, on Thursday as he outlined plans to expand a South Korean naval mission into waters south of Oman, closer to the Strait of Hormuz.

Cho said the move was intended to protect South Korean nationals and economic interests, according to Seoul’s foreign ministry.

South Korea’s parliamentary defense committee approved a motion to extend the Cheonghae anti-piracy unit’s deployment off Somalia and expand its patrol area.

The motion would add a maritime patrol aircraft and a team to dispose of explosives, while barring the unit from taking part in military operations between countries.

Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei urged the Basij paramilitary force on Thursday to mobilize those who share its outlook but have never formally joined, pointing to supporters who carry flags at state rallies.

In a written message marking Basij Week, Khamenei said the force “must undergo a transformation and rebirth.”

He also said the force “must draw on this newly awakened nation to develop and manage newer, more advanced versions of the Basij.”

“From now on, we must take bold, firm and deliberate steps toward making the slogan ‘every Iranian a Basij member’ a reality,” Khamenei wrote.

He also praised them for passing up “no opportunity to strike at the enemies of Islam and the Islamic system.”
